title: UI Designer Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: UI Designer.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas
lines: 1. Visual Design Principles: Typography scale, color theory and contrast ratios, spacing systems (8pt grid), hierarchy, and gestalt principles.
2. Design Systems: Component architecture in Figma (auto layout, variants, tokens), maintaining consistency across a product, and contributing to and consuming shared libraries.
3. Responsive & Adaptive Design: Breakpoint strategy, fluid vs. fixed layouts, component behavior across screen sizes, and dark/light mode support.
4. Handoff & Implementation Awareness: Writing developer-ready specs, understanding CSS constraints, working with engineers on feasibility, and using inspect tools accurately.

sections.heading: Question Strategy
lines: - Do not use a fixed sequence. Choose the next question based on the candidate's latest answer quality and identified gaps.
- Design system fluency and developer collaboration are the highest-signal areas for UI roles - probe for concrete examples.
- Use interview difficulty to calibrate: visual principles for entry-level, design system architecture and scalability for senior.
- Use resume and job-description signals to focus on the candidate's tooling (Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD) and product domain.
- If no job description is provided, do not infer or fabricate JD-specific requirements.
- If the candidate is strong in one area, shift to another high-signal UI design competency to broaden assessment.
